extractedItems.title: Where to drop a ball intentionally deflected by a person
extractedItems.question: If your ball is intentionally stopped by a person (not on the green), where should you drop it?

choices.text: At your original hitting spot
Within 1 club-length of where it would have come to rest
Anywhere on the fairway
Near the nearest point of relief

extractedItems.explanation: The ball must be dropped within 1 club-length of the estimated spot it would have come to rest without being deflected.
extractedItems.imagePrompt: A teenage boy golfer, right-handed, standing on the fairway next to a golf ball, ready to drop the ball after it was intentionally stopped by a person.
extractedItems.imageAlt: A golfer on the fairway preparing to drop a ball after it was intentionally stopped by a person.

extractedItems.title: Exception for balls intentionally deflected on the green
extractedItems.question: What should be done if a ball on the green is intentionally deflected after a stroke?

choices.text: Drop the ball within 1 club-length from the estimated spot
Place the ball where it was deflected
Replay the stroke
Play the ball as it lies

extractedItems.explanation: If the ball is intentionally deflected after a stroke on the green, the player must replay the stroke.
extractedItems.imagePrompt: A teenage girl golfer, left-handed, on the putting green preparing to replay her stroke after her ball was intentionally stopped.
extractedItems.imageAlt: A girl golfer on the green preparing to replay a putt after the ball was intentionally stopped.

extractedItems.title: Penalty for intentionally deflecting a moving ball
extractedItems.question: If someone intentionally stops or deflects a ball in motion, how many penalty strokes do they get?

choices.text: 1 penalty stroke
2 penalty strokes
Loss of hole
No penalty

extractedItems.explanation: A person who intentionally deflects or stops a moving ball gets 2 penalty strokes.
extractedItems.imagePrompt: A teenage boy golfer, right-handed, with another person standing close to his ball, indicating the ball has just been deflected in motion.
extractedItems.imageAlt: A boy golfer and another person near a moving ball that was intentionally stopped.

extractedItems.title: Objects as ball stoppers
extractedItems.question: Which of the following counts as intentional deflection of a moving golf ball?

choices.text: A person kicking the ball
A club dropped by accident blocking the ball
A water bottle purposefully put to stop the ball
The wind blowing the ball off course

extractedItems.explanation: Intentionally kicking the ball or placing an object to stop it both count as intentional deflection.
extractedItems.imagePrompt: A teenage girl golfer, right-handed, seeing her golf ball hit a deliberately placed water bottle on the fairway.
extractedItems.imageAlt: A girl golfer watches as her ball strikes a water bottle on the fairway that was purposefully placed as a stopper.

reviewedItems.title: Where to drop a ball intentionally deflected by a person

choices.text: At your original hitting spot
Within 1 club-length of where it would have come to rest
Anywhere on the fairway
At the point where it was struck

reviewedItems.explanation: If your ball is intentionally stopped or deflected by a person (not on the green), you must drop a ball within 1 club-length of the estimated spot where it would have come to rest.

reviewedItems.title: Exception for balls intentionally deflected on the green
reviewedItems.question: If your ball is on the putting green and is intentionally stopped or deflected after a stroke, what is the correct procedure?

choices.text: Drop a ball within 1 club-length from the estimated spot
Place the ball where it was deflected
Replay the stroke
Play the ball as it lies

reviewedItems.explanation: If your ball played from the green is intentionally deflected or stopped, the stroke is cancelled and you must replay the shot.

choices.text: 1 penalty stroke
2 penalty strokes
Loss of hole
No penalty

reviewedItems.explanation: A player who deliberately stops or deflects their own ball in motion receives the general penalty of two strokes.

reviewedItems.title: Objects as ball stoppers
reviewedItems.question: In which of these situations does it count as intentional deflection of a golf ball in motion?

choices.text: A person kicks the golf ball on purpose
A club dropped by accident blocks the ball
Someone puts a water bottle in the ball's path to stop it
The wind blows the ball in another direction

reviewedItems.explanation: Intentional actions, like kicking the ball or placing an object to stop it, count as intentional deflection. Accidents or natural influences like wind do not.
